questions.statement: Which of these is a vegetable?

options.feedback: Incorrect. Apple is a fruit.
Correct! Carrot is a common vegetable.
Incorrect. Chicken is meat/protein.
Incorrect. Bread is a carbohydrate/grain.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies basic food vocabulary and categories.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which food is a good source of protein?

options.feedback: Incorrect. Rice is a carbohydrate.
Incorrect. Lettuce is a vegetable.
Correct! Eggs are a well-known source of protein.
Incorrect. Candy is mostly sugar.

questions.explanation:
The student identifies specific food items associated with nutritional groups.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "Drinking ________ is better for your health than drinking soda."

options.feedback: Incorrect. While possible, water is the standard "healthy" alternative to soda.
Correct! Water is the healthiest option for hydration.
Incorrect. Milkshakes often have a lot of sugar, like soda.
Incorrect. Energy drinks are often less healthy than soda.

questions.explanation:
The student understands the health implications associated with different beverage choices.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "I am hungry between classes. I want a healthy snack. I should eat ________."

options.feedback: Incorrect. Chips are processed and often high in salt.
Correct! Fruit is a natural and healthy snack.
Incorrect. This is high in sugar.
Incorrect. This is a dessert, usually high in calories and sugar.

questions.explanation:
The student understands and applies the concept of "healthy" to food choices in a daily scenario.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "You should ________ eat fruits and vegetables to stay strong."

options.feedback: Incorrect. This would be unhealthy.
Incorrect. For good health, "always" or "every day" is better.
Correct! Regular consumption of fruits and vegetables is recommended for health.
Incorrect. This means almost never.

questions.explanation:
The student applies frequency adverbs to common health recommendations.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the main ingredient of 'Arepa'?
questions.context:
A description of a Colombian breakfast.
"In Colombia, many people eat 'Arepa' for breakfast. It is made of corn. They often have it with cheese and a cup of hot chocolate or coffee."

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says it's made of corn.
Incorrect. Cheese is an accompaniment.
Correct! The text says "It is made of corn".
Incorrect. This is a drink mentioned.

questions.explanation:
The student applies reading strategies to identify a specific factual detail in a cultural context.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "A balanced plate should have a ________ of protein, carbohydrates, and vegetables."

options.feedback: Incorrect. Having "a lot" of everything might lead to overeating.
Correct! A "balance" or "mixture" is the key to healthy eating.
Incorrect. You need enough of each to be healthy.
Incorrect. You need all three.

questions.explanation:
The student applies nutritional concepts to select the most appropriate word to describe a healthy diet.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the most likely cause of Lucas's low energy?
questions.context:
Analyzing a person's diet.
"Lucas loves fast food. He eats hamburgers three times a week and never eats salad. He feels tired and has low energy."

options.feedback: Incorrect. He never eats salad.
Incorrect. Not mentioned in the text.

options.text: His diet lacks essential nutrients from healthy foods.
options.feedback: Correct! Fast food is often low in nutrients, and he doesn't eat vegetables.
Incorrect. Not mentioned.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the relationship between dietary habits and physical consequences described in the text.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the words correctly?
questions.context: Distinguishing between healthy and unhealthy descriptors.

options.text: Junk food is very nutritious and good for your heart.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Junk food is the opposite of nutritious.

options.text: Fresh fruits are very nutritious and provide vitamins.
options.feedback: Correct! "Nutritious" and "vitamins" correctly describe fresh fruits.

options.text: Fried chicken is the most healthy way to eat protein.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Frying is generally less healthy than other methods.

options.text: Sugar gives you long-lasting energy for the whole day.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Sugar usually gives a short burst of energy followed by a crash.

questions.explanation:
The student analyzes the accuracy of statements combining food items and health descriptors.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Should a student who wants to be healthy buy this drink?
questions.context:
Evaluating a food advertisement.
"Try our new 'Mega-Choco-Shake'! It has 50 grams of sugar and only 2 grams of protein. It tastes like heaven!"

options.text: Yes, because it tastes like heaven.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Taste doesn't make it healthy.

options.text: Yes, because it has some protein.
options.feedback: Incorrect. 2 grams is very little compared to 50 grams of sugar.

options.text: No, because it contains an excessive amount of sugar.
options.feedback: Correct! 50 grams of sugar is very high and unhealthy.
Incorrect. Being "new" is not a health-related reason.

questions.explanation: The student evaluates the nutritional information provided in a simulated advertisement to make a healthy decision.
